entities.name: California State University, Northridge
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
California State University, Northridge (CSUN, founded 1958) is a public university in the San Fernando Valley area of Los Angeles, California — and the campus associated with one of the most significant events in American earthquake history: the 1994 Northridge earthquake (magnitude 6.7), which caused catastrophic damage to the university and fundamentally changed American understanding of earthquake engineering and seismic building design. CSUN's destruction and reconstruction after the earthquake has influenced building codes and seismic engineering standards nationwide.

The January 17, 1994, Northridge earthquake caused extensive structural damage to CSUN's campus, collapsing the parking structure and damaging many buildings, resulting in the tragic death of two campus employees. The university's rapid reconstruction (returning to full operation within months despite massive damage) was itself a remarkable achievement, and the lessons learned from CSUN's building damage patterns were incorporated into significantly revised California and national seismic building codes. CSUN's engineering department became a center of post-earthquake research.

CSUN serves approximately 38,000 students in the San Fernando Valley, which became increasingly Latino and immigrant-community dominant after the 1960s white flight to suburbs. The university has significant programs in business, arts, and sciences, and its National Center on Deafness is nationally recognized for deaf education services. CSUN has invested heavily in supporting students with disabilities, including deaf and hard-of-hearing students.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: California State University Northridge — whose catastrophic damage in the 1994 Northridge earthquake led to nationwide revision of seismic building codes, hosting the National Center on Deafness — is historically significant both as a seismic engineering landmark and a model of accessible education for diverse and disabled students.
